key_insight: To understand why language-model data attribution fails, evaluations need to separate the effects of different dataset properties. This paper introduces the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT) to investigate those effects through fact tracing.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations change multiple dataset properties at once, making it difficult to identify why an attribution method succeeds or fails at linking model outputs to training data.
method: Explore the design space of language-model data attribution, emphasizing evaluation.
Introduce CATT, a controlled benchmark for tracing facts back to training data.
Use controlled evaluation to disentangle potential sources of attribution failure; the supplied abstract is truncated before detailed procedures and results.
impact: More diagnostic evaluations could help practitioners select and improve attribution methods, rather than relying only on aggregate downstream performance. This supports clearer assessments of how reliably model outputs can be connected to training data.
visual_elements: Tracing diagram: training documents → language model → generated fact → attributed source.
Side-by-side comparison: evaluations with mixed dataset changes versus controlled evaluation.
Control-panel graphic showing dataset properties as independently adjustable knobs.
Diagnostic flowchart connecting an attribution failure to possible evaluation factors.
paper_title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
paper_authors: Steven Yu, Sheng-Yu Wang, Kimia Hamidieh, Antonio Torralba, David Bau
